Maya: Heads up — after yesterday's runtime rollout (attn-tiling + quant-profile v2) we see a sustained bump in prefix cache misses for a subset of production traffic. p99 latency +28% on text-gen routes that rely on cached prefixes.
Alex: saw the alert. Is this correlated with the new kernel selection policy?
Maya: seems tied to two changes: 1) tiling variant for attention that changes internal kv ordering, 2) quant profile flip from int8-a to int8-b which changed tensor layout for some ops. The cache keying is currently naive (raw token sequence + model build id).
Samir: can you paste a short profiler snippet? curious if there are cache lookup failures or just increased runtime per token.
Maya: pasted below (shortened):
```
[profiler] route: /v1/generate
avg_token_time: 12.4ms -> 15.8ms
kv_cache_lookup_rate: 87% -> 61%
kv_cache_miss_wave: 2024-04-03T18:02:24Z -> sustained
kernel_variant: attn_tiled_v3 -> attn_tiled_v4
quant_profile: int8-a -> int8-b
```
Jules: interesting — kv_cache_lookup_rate drop suggests key mismatch, not just perf of kernel. Could be key canonicalization changed (padding/seqlen ordering) in the tiled attention.
Maya: we confirmed a few failing keys: same prefix -> different internal cache key after compile. sample: `prefix_hash: a1b2c3` vs `prefix_hash: a1b2c3:tiling-v4` (we didn't expect a variant suffix).
Alex: that suffix being appended would def break cache. Where is that added? build-id? kernel metadata?
Samir: it's probably the kernel build fingerprint embedded in the compiled model metadata. The runtime concatenates model fingerprint + prefix hash for safety. If the new compiler stage started injecting a per-kernel sequence, the key changes.
Maya: timeline — we rolled runtime 2024-04-03 17:58 UTC, compiler switch happened on the same deploy. Ops-Bot noted compile artifact tag `attn_v4:tileOrder=col-major` in the deploy logs.
Ops-Bot: deploy #rdo-731 completed by @deploy-bot 2024-04-03T17:58:12Z. Artifacts: attn_tiled_v4, quant-int8-b.
Jules: quick mitigation: we can patch keying to ignore kernel artifact suffix for prefix cache keys (strip tiling metadata). That preserves safety if we keep the same logical model weights. But risk: a kernel variant could change semantics (ordering) — we need a compatibility check.
Alex: agree. Proposed steps: 1) put ephemeral toggle to prefer old keying for read path (so we look up both canonical and suffixed keys) 2) run A/B test on 10% traffic 3) run a deterministic compatibility test comparing outputs for a set of eval prompts.
Samir: I'll draft a PR for dual-read lookup (try suffixed, then fallback to canonical) and a metrics flag to count fallbacks. Also add a cache warmup job to re-populate canonical keys for the active prefix set.
Maya: can we get the A/B eval set? also want to check batching heuristics — we observed more small batches after rollout which exacerbates token p99. Might be scheduler picks attn_v4 more aggressively for short sequences.
Jules: scheduler change was in the same release — it now routes short sequences to the tiled kernel because it looked cheaper in microbenchmarks. But if it changes kv layout that's a problem. We'll gate that routing until compatibility verified.
Alex: timeline for mitigation? we should have a hotfix in <4h if possible. Ops — can you roll a small rollback if dual-read causes issues?
Ops-Bot: rollback playbook available: `deploy rollback --to rdo-730`. Manual approval required for Prod.
Samir: PR up in 10m. It implements dual-read, logs fallback counts to `prefix.cache.fallback_rate`. Also includes a background re-warm task that scans popular prefixes and writes canonical keys.
Maya: after PR I've run local sim on 5k prefixes — fallback_rate went from 42% -> 8% and p99 dropped ~12%. Good sign but need real traffic test.
Jules: add a quick compatibility job: run 1k eval prompts through both kernel variants and diff token outputs up to 128 tokens. If diffs > threshold, abort.
Alex: also check embedding/ordering in tokenizer normalization; earlier issues showed tokenization differences across model compile stages which can skew keys.
Maya: noted. I'll assemble tokenization diffs.
Samir: spinning up canary with dual-read + scheduler gate; tagging it canary/kv-fix. Will route 5% traffic.
Maya: thanks. If canary looks good, we can promote and schedule a safe rollout for kernel scheduler change with explicit compatibility gating.
Alex: follow-up: create an incident postmortem stub (brief) capturing root cause hypothesis (kernel metadata added to cache keys) and the mitigation steps. I can seed it after the canary results.
Maya: assigned. I'll report back in this thread with 30m, 2h, and postmortem link.
Samir: PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4823 (dual-read + rewarm).
Jules: good. If anyone sees new spikes, ping oncall. :phone:
Maya: thanks all — will update.
